summary: Lookout house built 1940-41 by CCC crews in the Lewis and Clark National Forest; listed as a camp, abandoned in the 1950s; remains not described.

facts.design: Lookout house (per a January 1941 newspaper item)
facts.status_note: firelookout.com says it was abandoned in the 1950s. The Forest Fire Lookout Association lists it as a camp, abandoned.

events.note: Construction began in summer 1940 with five CCC men under foreman Paul Hazel. The lookout house was 95 percent complete by January 1941.
firelookout.com gives only 'Abandoned 1950s'. The year 1950 stands in for the decade.

evidence.supports: Location: 37 miles WSW of Choteau, Lewis & Clark County
Listed as a camp in the 1940s and abandoned in the 1950s
June 1940 item: new lookout to be built that summer with five CCC men under Paul Hazel
evidence.quote: This is a new lookout to be constructed this summer, starting next week with five CCC men under Paul Hazel, foreman.

evidence.supports: The lookout sits on the ridge between Rock and Moose creeks
evidence.quote: The lookout lies on the ridge between Rock and Moose creeks.

evidence.supports: The June 1940 item calls the post the Lake View lookout
January 1941 report: lookout house 95 percent complete
evidence.quote: Moose Ridge - L-4 -- T-10 Lookout House - 95 percent complete.

evidence.supports: Telephone line to the lookout still had to be built
evidence.quote: To make the setup for the Moose Ridge Lookout complete, a telephone line from the lookout down to the Gates Park-Spotted Bear line will have to be constructed.

evidence.supports: Forest Fire Lookout Association lists Moose Ridge as a camp that is abandoned
evidence.quote: Lewis & Clark Moose Ridge 47.71451 -113.06077 Camp Abandoned

evidence.supports: The page also carries the single word Removed, with no date or explanation
Agency: Lewis and Clark National Forest
The June 1940 item is a newspaper item from The Choteau Acantha
The construction report is dated January 2, 1941

resolved_conflicts.explanation: firelookout.com and the Forest Fire Lookout Association list the site as a camp. The montanalookouts page describes a lookout house built by CCC crews in 1940-41. The story describes both.
The June 1940 item calls the post the Lake View lookout. The January 1941 item refers to the Moose Ridge Lookout. The story uses the brief's name, Moose Ridge.

notes_for_editor: Few sources and no current description of the site. The one-word 'Removed' at the foot of the montanalookouts page is unexplained, so the story does not say what it means. Brief coordinates (47.7367, -112.9894) are about 6 km from the Forest Fire Lookout Association point (47.71451, -113.06077); neither was checked against a Forest Service map, and the brief's coordinates were left unchanged. The brief's kind 'unknown' and status 'unknown' are answered by the sources as lookout house and abandoned. The 1940 item's 'Lake View' name and the 1941 'Moose Ridge Lookout' name are not reconciled by any source. No staffing dates are given.
